entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antigonus I Monophthalmus, a pivotal figure in the Hellenistic world, was a Macedonian Greek general and successor of Alexander the Great.

As a prominent military leader in Alexander's army, he controlled vast territories, including the former Persian satrapies of Bactria and Sogdiana, and the islands of Rhodes and Cyprus.

In 306 BC, he assumed the title of basileus (king) and reigned until his death in 300 BCE, marking the beginning of the Antigonid dynasty, which ruled over Macedonia until its conquest by the Roman Republic in 168 BC.

This dynasty's reign was characterized by a complex web of alliances and rivalries with neighboring kingdoms, including the Seleucid Empire and the Ptolemaic Kingdom.
